data.title: iOS Platform Support (v1.1+)
data.goalStatement: Extends the proven Android flow to iOS by implementing the platform switch's iOS branch over idb + simctl: simulator and physical-device discovery, live mirroring, screenshot and view-hierarchy capture, and the two iOS-specific error cards — simulator-not-booted ('Boot simulator' / 'Choose another') and device-not-trusted ("I've tapped Trust — retry" / 'Use simulator'). Reuses F-1's shell, F-4/F-5's annotation and measure surfaces, F-7's MCP handoff and F-9's Verify engine behind a platform abstraction, so only the device-adapter layer and the iOS error states are new. Why: deliberately deferred out of v1 (AS-5) so the complete Android loop ships first; it is the obvious parity follow-up once that loop is validated.

functionalRequirements.text: (v1.1+) Support iOS simulator/device mirroring via idb+simctl, including simulator-not-booted and device-not-trusted error-card states.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: adb/idb commands are only ever invoked against the user's explicitly selected, connected device — never an arbitrary or remote target.
Device picker, annotation popovers, and error-card actions are fully keyboard-navigable (arrow keys/Enter for pickers, Enter/Escape for popovers).
All screens support full light and dark theme parity using the defined signal-color system (red = bug, green = fixed, orange = warning, blue = measurement) with sufficient contrast in both themes.
v1 targets macOS only; no Windows/Linux builds.

acceptanceCriteria.text: (v1.1+) Given iOS is selected as platform, when the simulator isn't booted, then an error card with 'Boot simulator' primary / 'Choose another' secondary renders; when the device isn't trusted, an error card with "I've tapped Trust — retry" primary / 'Use simulator' secondary renders.

scenarios.title: (v1.1+) iOS simulator not booted / device not trusted
steps: Simulator not booted -> error card offers Boot simulator
Or device not trusted -> error card offers Trust-and-retry / Use simulator

userStories.iWant: (v1.1+) the same mirror/annotate/send flow against an iOS simulator or device
userStories.soThat: I can use one tool across both platforms my app ships on
